issues.description: Method name mismatch for clearing the stock: the problem statement UML declares Stock.emptyStock(): void, the template Stock class provides clearInventory(), while the solution Stock class implements emptyStock(). This inconsistency between template and specification can confuse students about which method to use/implement and may cause compilation or test failures if the expected method name differs.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either rename the template's clearInventory() method to emptyStock() to match the UML/specification and the solution, or update the problem statement/UML to reference clearInventory(). Ensure the chosen name is used in template, tests, and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) specifies a Stock method named emptyStock(), and the reference solution implements emptyStock(), but the template repository's Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This is the same conceptual operation (clearing/emptying the stock) under two different names across artifacts, which can confuse students when they look for the expected method to call/implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (or vice versa update problem and solution to clearInventory), so that the template, problem statement, and solution use the same identifier for the stock-clearing operation.
